question: Does the high-contention STAGED-over-DIRECT relationship at 5000 ns follower idle change between calibrated S, M, and H body costs?
requiredCalculations: For S and H separately, compute paired STAGED minus DIRECT throughput within every Williams block.
Report paired mean, median, sample standard deviation, range, percentage delta, and STAGED win count.
Carry forward the retained M-body 5000 ns STAGED-minus-DIRECT paired result without pooling it with new S/H runs.
Report treatment means and sample CV across independent JVM replicas for every action/body combination.
Report within-replica CV without treating measurement iterations as independent forks.
Classify every state-22-dominant measurement and retain its action, body, and block identity.
Determine whether the sign and practical magnitude of the STAGED-minus-DIRECT effect agree across S, M, and H.
Evaluate acquisition success, contention, idle fraction, and throughput jointly for each body row.
interpretationRules: Do not average contradictory body regimes into one policy conclusion.
If S, M, and H agree materially, treat STAGED / 5000 ns as the lower-dimensional candidate for later topology checks.
If one body reverses or becomes ambiguous, refine only that body row.
Do not add XS or XH unless S/H evidence specifically requires an endpoint.
Do not reopen skip or tune contention thresholds.
State 22 remains explanatory telemetry, not the primary ranking target.
stopRule: Stop after classifying body sensitivity and naming the minimum justified contention/topology sensitivity check. Do not configure or execute topology, P-core, skip, or threshold work.
